text.p: Pakistan's ousted prime minister refused on Tuesday to accept her crushing defeat in "engineered" elections, but said she had no plans to launch popular agitation against her victorious rival Nawaz Sharif.
She told a news conference she would propose to a Central Executive Committee meeting of her Pakistan People's Party (PPP) on Wednesday that the party "cooperate in creating stability".
Bhutto accused the caretaker government appointed by President Farooq Leghari of engineering Monday's elections to defeat her, saying: "I do not accept the result."

But she added: "Irrespective of my views concerning the legitimacy of the electoral process, I wish Mian Nawaz Sharif good luck. The country needs political stability, our people need economic relief. The two go hand in hand."

"At tomorrow's Central Executive meeting, I shall propose to my party to cooperate in creating stability in the country, which in the long run will strengthen democracy and the economic well-being of our people."

Leghari sacked Bhutto's government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule. Her PPP suffered humiliation at the polls -- with 185 results declared, the PPP had won only 17 seats in the 217-seat National Assembly against 127 for Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League.
